steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line cups with paper liners.
Whisk flour, cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice, nutmeg, ginger, salt, baking soda, allspice, cloves, and cardamom together in a bowl.

Beat brown sugar and eggs together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Beat in pumpkin purée and 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons vegetable oil until combined. Beat in flour mixture until just incorporated.

Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each about 1/2 full. Spoon about 1 teaspoon cream cheese into center of each muffin cup; poke it down into middle of batter. Sprinkle sunflower seeds over muffin tops.

Bake in the preheated oven until golden and tops spring back when lightly pressed, about 25 minutes. Cool muffins in tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. Be careful; the cream cheese stays hot for a while.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Cheese Filled Pumpkin Muffins
raw_recipe.description: This cream cheese-filled pumpkin muffins recipe is a straightforward recipe with a mix of spices like cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg, cardamom, and ginger.

review.reviewBody: If I could give this recipe more than 5 stars, I would, they are absolutely DELICIOUS! I made these exactly as written, except I topped mine with a walnut streusel topping before baking instead of just plain nuts. I loved how quick and easy these were to make too...just used a bowl and a whisk and they came together in a snap! I got 20 regular sized muffins out of the recipe and I baked them @ 325 for only 14 minutes (HOT oven). Laurrie, this recipe is PERFECT...Thanks for sharing. :)

These were amazing! I added 3 T powdered sugar and 1/2 tsp almond extract to the cream cheese, then used a small melon scooper to scoop the cream cheese into mini muffin tins, then froze them for about 30 minutes. They were so easy to put in between the muffin mix when they were partially frozen. So good! I will be making these again!

I made these muffins because of the dark brown sugar and spice combination. The spices were great and the muffins super moist. However, I was confused by the use of baking soda and no baking powder. Baking soda requires an acid in the recipe to work properly and I didn't see an acid listed in these ingredients-so I used 3/4 teaspoon of baking powder (more is required because the leavening power of baking soda is much greater than baking powder)and added 1/4 teaspoon baking soda. I increased the cream cheese to about 6 tablespoons, adding 3 tablespoons powdered sugar and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla. I then put a very thin layer of batter into my muffin cups, added a dollop of the cream cheese, and covered with the rest of the batter-the filling stayed in the middle of the muffins this way. Finally, I added a streusel topping as others have suggested made with 1/3 cup brown sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1 tablespoon butter because I wanted to add some more sweetness. I left off the sunflower seeds. The topping MADE the muffins and was definitely my favorite part. This produced 15, not 12, beautiful muffins, and, as I have found with all pumpkin bread recipes, the flavor improves the next day.

Truly outstanding--a huge hit with everyone. Except for the cardamom, which I didn't have and didn't want to spend $ on, I followed recipe exactly. It was perfectly spiced without it. Tips:
1. I knew before I read the reviews that the cream cheese needed doctoring. I added 1/4 cup powdered sugar and 1/2 tsp almond extra as others suggested. Superb.
2. The muffin texture is lovely with moisture, but at first touch you can feel the oiliness--next time I will reduce the total oil by 2 tablespoons.
3. The streusel topping written up by TheBritishBaker (reviewer) gives a nice crispy texture to the top: 1/3 cup brown sugar; 2 tablespoons flour; 1/8 tsp cinnamon; 1 tablespoon butter. I put it in a food processor. Quick and perfectly blended, then just sprinkle over top before baking. Makes the muffins pretty too.
4. Can't remember who suggested it, but the notion of rolling the cream cheese/sugar/extract into a slender log and freezing it 30 mins works very well. I cut the log into 12 identical blobs and quickly rolled them into little balls (the powdered sugar makes this possible). I pressed a little ball into the half-filled muffin cup, giving it a tiny shove to push it down a bit, then covered it with more muffin batter. This method turned out 12 identical muffins, generously sized, and the cream cheese center was beautifully round shaped and perfectly centered. I used standard muffin cups, not the really big or really small ones. 
This is definitely a keeper. We love them!

Everyone loved these muffins! I will definitely be using this recipe again! I did substitute 1 cup butter for the oil. I used chopped frozen cranberries, which always add moistness to everything they’re baked in. I also added ( 2 squares) white almond bark (shredded). And topped them with a strudel made of oats, pecans, brown sugar and coconut. The cream cheese I mixed with 1/4 c white sugar, almond extract and a splash of southern comfort. I had leftover ingredients from Christmas baking, so I used some of them up. Thank you for sharing the original recipe and to everyone who left reviews an suggestions. I look forward to doing this again and going for a healthier option.

So delicious! Definitely a new favorite recipe I plan to make many times a year!!! I made a few modifications based on some other reviews and some of my own. I substituted the vege oil for natural applesauce, I used 3/4 cup (lightly packed) brown sugar I substituted baking soda for 1.5 tsps of baking powder, I also have a gluten allergy and used brown rice flour. For the cream cheese filling I used 8 ozs(I wanted more than a tsp of cream cheese filling), I sweetened it with 2 tsps of confectioners sugar and 1/2 tsp vanilla. 
I filled regular size muffin cups a little less than half way, then I added the cream cheese, I then added more pumpkin mixture on top until muffin cup was filled. 
I opted to use crushed pecans, brown sugar (btwn 1/4-1/3 cup of each) and butter (about 1 tbsp, melted))mixed together with my fingers for my topping. 
Mine only took about 18 minutes to bake. I got 14 muffins out of the mixture.The minute they can out of the oven both my husband and I enjoyed one :)

Love This Recipe! I made it in an 8x8 in square pan (put most batter in, dollop in cream cheese, then dollop over with remaining batter) . As other reviewers, I used 8 oz cream cheese and 1 c powdered sugar. Also used about 1/3 of flour as whole wheat flour. When I make again I might try adding some egg to the cream cheese to lighten it, but might not. Its really good and just as good a few days later. We use it for breakfast or wrap and take for snack at work. If you like pumpkin pie you will Love this.

Delicious! After reading a few of the reviews I decided to sweeten the cream cheese. I added 1/2 cup powdered sugar to 4 oz of the cream cheese. I filled the cupcake tin 1/2 full of pumpkin mixture, added 1/2 tbs. of cream cheese and added topped it with more pumpkin mixture to cover the cream cheese. I'm not a fan of sunflower seeds, so I made a streusel topping of 1/2 cup of flower, 1/4 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 tsp. cinnamon, and 1/2 stick of softened butter. I combined them with my fingers and crumbled the mixture on top of the cupcake. Bake for 25 minutes at 350 and they came out perfect! Not too gooey, but dry enough to be considered a muffin and not a cupcake.

I too am a huge fan of Starbucks pumpkin cream cheese muffins. However, they are rather costly. To make these more healthy I used freshly ground soft whole wheat flour in place of most of the AP flour. You could not tell at all since the pumpkin flavor overwhelms the wheat. Also, I followed the advice of another reviewer and froze the cream cheese filling. I simply used my cookie scoop and dropped the cream cheese filling on a plate and froze it. Wonderful! I had perfect cream cheese centers! Also, remembering not to beat the cream cheese until it is soup makes all the difference. It should keep its form when scooped otherwise you beat it too long! Wonderful muffins, thank you for sharing!!!

These were really good muffins. I added a little powdered sugar to the cream cheese. I found that it was easier to fill the muffin cups part way, add the cream cheese, and then put another spoon of the batter on top. This keeps your cream cheese at the center instead of at the top of your muffins. Next time I will double the cream cheese mixture so that I have more of it in the middle. Thanks for a great recipe!

First I would like to say I really appreciate all the comments, I found them very helpful when making these. The only changes I made is using un-sweetened applesauce instead of oil, added 1 cup of raisins and used a pecan and brown sugar topping. After seeing all of the comments about the cream cheese filling, I used the following for mine: 8 oz cream cheese, 2 tsp. vanilla, 1 egg yolk and 1/4 cup of white sugar. They turned out absolutely delicious! Thank you so much for posting this yummy recipe!

They are good but I agree with the others saying that they might need baking powder, they don't rise very much and are not fluffy, and that they are not very sweet, might be good to add some sugar to the cream cheese. They are good but there's definitely room for improvement.
I loved this recipe I just think it would be better without cream cheese.
These muffins are always a big hit! I top them with Trader Joes pumpkin spiced pumpkin seeds

I made these muffins and they were pretty good. Cream cheese filling makes them what they are: delicious. I don't understand the many people who rate this recipe and then listed the changes they made - you can't accurately rate the recipe if you've changed it!

As many others recommended, I added a couple of tablespoons of powdered sugar to the cream cheese, and then also added the zest of one orange before filling the muffins .... it was a nice combination! The muffins looked a bit plain so I added some chopped walnuts to the top before baking and this really helped.

As I was gathering the dry ingredients I realized it had no baking powder, so I added 1 1\2 tsp . Don't know if she forgot it or what but they turned out well and my husband said they were very good . I also noticed that the cream cheese just stayed pretty much on top not in the middle as pictured but was still very good . Maybe I didn't push it far enough down in the batter.
I added mini chocolate chips on top instead of sunflower seeds.

These are great!! We like using as little sugar as possible, so here are the changes I made.... 2/3 cup sugar only, & cut the oil to 1 cup. I added 1 tsp of vanilla to the cream cheese. We are touchy with some spices so I used the pumpkin pie spice, 1/2 the cinnamon, and just a pinch of clove. Many of the other spices in the recipe are already in the pumpkin pie spice, so I omitted them.
I omitted the seeds and I whipped the cream cheese with cinnamon and sugar before stuffing the muffins. Very moist and delicious!
